extracted.intended_audience: readers and fans of stand-up comedy; people interested in comedy criticism/reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or writing a review of a live stand-up comedy performance or recording, focusing on material, delivery, audience interaction, and emotional effect. Emphasizes how personal/troubling subject matter is handled in a comedic context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening hook / startling first line
rubrics_metrics.description: Notaro began her set... by saying, 'Good evening, hello. I have cancer. How are you?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer highlights the power of a striking, candid opening that immediately establishes stakes and tone; a good opening can shock, orient the audience, and set up the emotional territory of the set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of personal tragedy as comic material
rubrics_metrics.description: With humor, the equation is tragedy plus time equals comedy; 'I am just at tragedy, right now,' Notaro says.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the performer can turn recent personal tragedy into material without trivializing it — honest acknowledgement of current trauma can be part of the act, and being 'at tragedy' differs from finished comedic processing. Consider sensitivity, honesty, and whether jokes arise naturally from the experience rather than exploiting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: The sense that this deeply personal material is still taking shape; intimate, raw moments throughout the set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether material feels genuinely lived-in and vulnerable rather than performative. Authenticity includes revealing personal details, emotional candor, and a lack of artificial polish that lets listeners feel they're witnessing real processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimate interactions with the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: These intimate interactions with the audience are a lot of what makes Tig Notaro: Live an amazing listen. Notaro tries to comfort one audience member... admonishes another: 'Sir, this should not tickle you so much.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the quality of direct address, reader comfort-building, and management of audience responses. Good interactions can deepen emotional texture, create empathy, and provide comic beats; poor handling of reactions (ignoring, defensive, or tone-deaf responses) can spoil material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roughness / 'tryout' quality vs polished craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The other is the roughness around the edges, the sense that this deeply personal material is still taking shape; 'A perfectly polished and crafted standup set can be a beautiful thing... but it’s rare to hear... the rough-hewn tryout of material you get here.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether roughness helps (feels immediate, honest) or hurts (unfinished, unfocused). The reviewer values hearing material in mid-development when it communicates risk and discovery; polished sets are compared as a different (also valid) aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone shifts and pacing (from laughter to quiet realization)
rubrics_metrics.description: After she describes finding a lump and going to the hospital, it gets quieter, and you can tell that the realization is settling in that she isn’t kidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timing and control of tonal transitions: being able to move an audience from nervous laughter to silence to empathy is a skill. Effective pacing lets the emotional truth land and maximizes both comic and poignant moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of riffs and concrete comic bits
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes about a questionnaire the hospital sent to her mother... a story about being mistaken for a man... riffs about cancer greeting cards, wanting to date after the diagnosis, and encouraging her friends to speak to her like a normal person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the quality of specific comedic material — the strength of premises, development of riffs, originality, and the way concrete anecdotes illuminate themes. Bits that are both funny and revealing score highly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing anger and hilarity ('raw, angry hilarity')
rubrics_metrics.description: There are raw, angry hilarity moments — angry/frank responses to bureaucratic or absurd elements around tragedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for how the performer channels anger or outrage into comedy without losing nuance. Anger can be a rich comedic resource when it feels justified and is transformed into clever observation or righteous punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise, juxtaposition, and finding pathos in mundane details
rubrics_metrics.description: A surprising amount of pathos in a joke about traffic after hearing someone discuss getting cancer, ending a relationship, and losing a parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the performer’s ability to create emotional contrast and find unexpected poignancy in everyday observations. Effective comedy can gain power from juxtaposing the trivial and the tragic to produce bittersweet or resonant laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional risk-taking and confronting inappropriate responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Addressing an audience member who laughs inappropriately: 'Sir, this should not tickle you so much. I’m not that happy and comfortable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess willingness to call out or manage uncomfortable audience behavior and to take on subjects that might provoke uneasy laughter. Risk-taking that maintains control and purpose enhances the set; mishandling can derail tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact: riveting, moving, occasionally hilarious
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after all the build-up online, it makes for a riveting, moving, occasionally hilarious 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the set's cumulative effect on the listener: does it move you, hold attention, provoke laughter, and leave a lasting impression? A strong set integrates its parts into a coherent emotional and comedic arc.
